title: Who should change groups?
hook: Move one unchanged score between groups and recompute both averages.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: move one person between groups and both group averages rise.

misconception: Treating will rogers effect as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: move one person between groups and both group averages rise.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Group A has scores 1,2 and B has 3,4,9. Move score 3 from B into A without changing any score. What happens to both group means?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-will-rogers-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Group A [1,2] mean1.5, B [3,4,9] mean5.3333. Move3 from B to A: Amean2, Bmean6.5. Individual scores unchanged; both group averages rise.

src/demos/probability/p100-will-rogers-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Group A [1,2] mean1.5, B [3,4,9] mean5.3333. Move3 from B to A: Amean2, Bmean6.5. Individual scores unchanged; both group averages rise.

claims.text: After reassignment the retained means are 2 and 6.5, versus 1.5 and 5.333 in the original groups. Score 3 is above A’s old mean and below B’s old mean.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-will-rogers-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Group A [1,2] mean1.5, B [3,4,9] mean5.3333. Move3 from B to A: Amean2, Bmean6.5. Individual scores unchanged; both group averages rise.

claims.text: Adding it raises A’s mean, and removing it raises B’s mean. No individual improved: group membership changed. Both group summaries can improve while the combined population remains identical.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-will-rogers-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Group A [1,2] mean1.5, B [3,4,9] mean5.3333. Move3 from B to A: Amean2, Bmean6.5. Individual scores unchanged; both group averages rise.

claims.text: Move a score above the receiving group’s mean and below the sending group’s mean. What happens? The moved score pulls the receiving mean up, and its removal pulls the sending mean up.

provenance.difference: New teaching boundary: Will Rogers effect. Existing boundary: The learner can explain that when a person chooses who is treated, whatever guides the choice (here fitness) shows up as a treatment effect, and that random assignment spreads it evenly over both groups.
